d.description: The `d` [CSS](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS) property defines a path to be drawn by the SVG `path` element. If present, it overrides the element's `d` attribute.

values.none: No path is drawn.

direction.description: The `direction` [CSS](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS) property sets the direction of text, table and grid columns, and horizontal overflow. Use `rtl` for languages written from right to left (like Hebrew or Arabic), and `ltr` for those written from left to right (like English and most other languages).

values.ltr: Text and other elements go from left to right. This is the default value.
values.rtl: Text and other elements go from right to left.

display.description: The `display` [CSS](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS) property sets whether an element is treated as a [block or inline box](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Guides/Display/Flow_layout) and the layout used for its children, such as [flow layout](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Guides/Display/Flow_layout), [grid](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Guides/Grid_layout) or [flex](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Guides/Flexible_box_layout).

values.flow-root: The element generates a block box that establishes a new [block formatting context](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Guides/Display/Block_formatting_context), defining where the formatting root lies. - `table` - : These elements behave like HTML `table` elements. It defines a block-level box. - `flex` - : The element behaves like a block-level element and lays out its content according to the [flexbox model](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Guides/Flexible_box_layout). - `grid` - : The element behaves like a block-level element and lays out its content according to the [grid model](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Guides/Grid_layout/Basic_concepts). - `grid-lanes` - : The element behaves like a block-level element and lays out its content using grid lanes layout. Columns are defined by `grid-template-columns` and behave like a strict grid, while items are packed in the block direction to fill gaps between items of different sizes. See [Grid lanes layout](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Guides/Grid_layout/Grid_lanes) for details. - `ruby` - : The element behaves like an inline-level element and lays out its content according to the ruby formatting model. It behaves like the corresponding HTML `ruby` elements.
values.none: Turns off the display of an element so that it has no effect on layout (the document is rendered as though the element did not exist). All descendant elements also have their display turned off. To have an element take up the space that it would normally take, but without actually rendering anything, use the `visibility` property instead.
values.inline-table: The `inline-table` value does not have a direct mapping in HTML. It behaves like an HTML `table` element, but as an inline box, rather than a block-level box. Inside the table box is a block-level context.
values.inline-flex: The element behaves like an inline-level element and lays out its content according to the flexbox model.
values.inline-grid: The element behaves like an inline-level element and lays out its content according to the grid model.
values.inline-grid-lanes: The element behaves like an inline-level element and lays out its content using grid lanes layout. Rows are defined by `grid-template-rows` and behave like a strict grid, while items are packed in the inline direction to fill gaps between items of different sizes. See [Grid lanes layout](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Guides/Grid_layout/Grid_lanes) for details.
values.block: The element generates a block-level box
values.contents: The element itself does not generate any boxes, but its children and pseudo-elements still generate boxes as normal.
values.flex: The element generates a principal flex container box and establishes a flex formatting context.
values.flexbox: The element lays out its contents using flow layout (block-and-inline layout). Standardized as 'flex'.
values.grid: The element generates a principal grid container box, and establishes a grid formatting context.
values.inline: The element generates an inline-level box.
values.inline-block: A block box, which itself is flowed as a single inline box, similar to a replaced element. The inside of an inline-block is formatted as a block box, and the box itself is formatted as an inline box.
values.list-item: One or more block boxes and one marker box.
values.-moz-box: The element lays out its contents using flow layout (block-and-inline layout). Standardized as 'flex'.
values.-ms-flexbox: The element lays out its contents using flow layout (block-and-inline layout). Standardized as 'flex'.
values.-ms-grid: The element generates a principal grid container box, and establishes a grid formatting context.
values.ruby: The element generates a principal ruby container box, and establishes a ruby formatting context.
values.run-in: The element generates a run-in box. Run-in elements act like inlines or blocks, depending on the surrounding elements.
values.table: The element generates a principal table wrapper box containing an additionally-generated table box, and establishes a table formatting context.
values.-webkit-box: The element lays out its contents using flow layout (block-and-inline layout). Standardized as 'flex'.
values.-webkit-flex: The element lays out its contents using flow layout (block-and-inline layout).
values.flow: The element lays out its contents using flow layout (block-and-inline layout).
values.table-row-group: These elements behave like `tbody` HTML elements.
values.table-header-group: These elements behave like `thead` HTML elements.
values.table-footer-group: These elements behave like `tfoot` HTML elements.
values.table-row: These elements behave like `tr` HTML elements.
values.table-cell: These elements behave like `td` HTML elements.
values.table-column-group: These elements behave like `colgroup` HTML elements.
values.table-column: These elements behave like `col` HTML elements.
values.table-caption: These elements behave like `caption` HTML elements.
values.ruby-base: These elements behave like `rb` HTML elements.
values.ruby-text: These elements behave like `rt` HTML elements.
values.ruby-base-container: These elements are generated as anonymous boxes.
values.ruby-text-container: These elements behave like `rtc` HTML elements.

dominant-baseline.description: The `dominant-baseline` [CSS](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS) property specifies the specific [baseline](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Glossary/Baseline/Typography) used to align the box's text and inline-level contents. It also indicates the default alignment baseline of any boxes participating in baseline alignment in the box's alignment context. If present, it overrides the shape's `dominant-baseline` attribute.

values.auto: If this property is applied to a `text` element, then the computed value depends on the value of the `writing-mode` attribute.
values.alphabetic: The baseline-identifier for the dominant-baseline is set to be `alphabetic`, the derived baseline-table is constructed using the `alphabetic` baseline-table in the font, and the baseline-table font-size is changed to the value of the element's `font-size` SVG attribute or the CSS `font-size`, if set.
values.central: The baseline-identifier for the dominant-baseline is set to be `central`. The derived baseline-table is constructed from the defined baselines in the font's baseline-table. That font baseline-table is chosen using the following priority order of baseline-table names: `ideographic`, `alphabetic`, `hanging`, `mathematical`. The baseline-table font-size is changed to the value of the element's `font-size` SVG attribute or the CSS `font-size`, if set.
values.hanging: The baseline-identifier for the dominant-baseline is set to be `hanging`, the derived baseline-table is constructed using the `hanging` baseline-table in the font, and the baseline-table font-size is changed to the value of the `font-size` SVG attribute of `font-size` CSS property on this element.
values.ideographic: The baseline-identifier for the dominant-baseline is set to be `ideographic`, the derived baseline-table is constructed using the `ideographic` baseline-table in the font, and the baseline-table font-size is changed to the value of the value of the element's `font-size` SVG attribute or the CSS `font-size`, if set.
values.mathematical: The baseline-identifier for the dominant-baseline is set to be `mathematical`, the derived baseline-table is constructed using the `mathematical` baseline-table in the font, and the baseline-table font-size is changed to the value of the value of the element's `font-size` SVG attribute or the CSS `font-size`, if set.
values.middle: The baseline-identifier for the dominant-baseline is set to be `middle`. The derived baseline-table is constructed from the defined baselines in a baseline-table in the font. That font baseline-table is chosen using the following priority order of baseline-table names: `ideographic`, `alphabetic`, `hanging`, `mathematical`. The baseline-table font-size is changed to the value of the element's `font-size` SVG attribute or the CSS `font-size`, if set.
values.text-bottom: The _line-under_ edge is used as the baseline, which is usually the bottom edge of the font's em box.
values.text-top: The _line-over_ edge is used as the baseline, which is usually the top edge of the font's em box.

dynamic-range-limit.description: The `dynamic-range-limit` [CSS](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS) property specifies the maximum luminance allowed for High Dynamic Range (HDR) content.

values.standard: Specifies the maximum luminance as High Dynamic Range (HDR) reference white, which is the CSS color `white`.
values.no-limit: Specifies the maximum luminance as much greater than that of HDR reference white. The precise level is not specified. This is the initial value.
values.constrained: Specifies the maximum luminance as somewhat greater than that of HDR reference white, such that a mix of Standard Dynamic Range (SDR) and HDR content can be comfortably viewed together. The precise level is not specified.

empty-cells.description: The `empty-cells` [CSS](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS) property sets whether borders and backgrounds appear around `table` cells that have no visible content.

values.show: Borders and backgrounds are drawn like in normal cells.
values.hide: No borders or backgrounds are drawn.

field-sizing.description: The `field-sizing` [CSS](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS) property enables you to control the sizing behavior of elements that are given a default preferred size, such as form control elements. This property enables you to override the default sizing behavior, allowing form controls to adjust in size to fit their contents.

values.content: Allows the element to adjust its size to fit its contents.
values.fixed: Sets a fixed size for the element. This is the default value.

fill.description: The `fill` [CSS](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS) property defines how SVG text content and the interior canvas of SVG shapes are filled or painted. If present, it overrides the element's `fill` attribute.

values.none: No `fill` is painted; the areas inside the stroke, if any, are transparent.
values.context-fill: Uses the paint value of `fill` from a context element.
values.context-stroke: Uses the paint value of `stroke` from a context element.
values.url(): A URL reference to a paint server element, which is an element that defines a paint server: 'hatch', 'linearGradient', 'mesh', 'pattern', 'radialGradient' and 'solidcolor'.

fill-opacity.description: The `fill-opacity` [CSS](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS) property defines the opacity of the painting operation (color, gradient, pattern, etc.) applied to SVG shapes or text content elements to fill the element. The property defines the opacity of the element's `fill` only; it does not affect the stroke. If present, it overrides the element's `fill-opacity` attribute.

fill-rule.description: The `fill-rule` [CSS](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS) property defines the rule used to determine which parts of the SVG shape's canvas are included inside a shape to be filled. If present, it overrides the element's `fill-rule` attribute.

values.nonzero: For every point in the shape, a ray is drawn in a random direction to beyond the shape's outer edges. Each ray is examined to determine the places where the ray crosses the shape. Starting with a count of zero, add one each time a path segment crosses the ray from left to right and subtract one each time a path segment crosses the ray from right to left. After counting the crossings, if the result is zero then the point is outside the path. Otherwise, it is inside.
values.evenodd: For every point in the fill rule's box, a ray is drawn in a random direction. The number of path segments from the given shape that the ray crosses are counted. If this number is odd, the point is inside; if even, the point is outside. Zero is taken to be even.

filter.description: The `filter` [CSS](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS) property applies graphical effects like blur or color shift to an element. Filters are commonly used to adjust the rendering of images, backgrounds, and borders.

values.none: No filter effects are applied.
values.blur(): Applies a Gaussian blur to the input image.
values.brightness(): Applies a linear multiplier to input image, making it appear more or less bright.
values.contrast(): Adjusts the contrast of the input.
values.drop-shadow(): Applies a drop shadow effect to the input image.
values.grayscale(): Converts the input image to grayscale.
values.hue-rotate(): Applies a hue rotation on the input image.
values.invert(): Inverts the samples in the input image.
values.opacity(): Applies transparency to the samples in the input image.
values.sepia(): Converts the input image to sepia.
values.url(): A filter reference to a <filter> element.

flex.description: The `flex` [CSS](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS) [shorthand](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Guides/Cascade/Shorthand_properties) property sets how a `flex item` will grow or shrink to fit the space available in its flex container.

values.none: The item is sized according to its `width` and `height` properties. It is fully inflexible: it neither shrinks nor grows in relation to the flex container. This is equivalent to setting `flex: 0 0 auto`.
values.auto: Retrieves the value of the main size property as the used 'flex-basis'.
values.content: Indicates automatic sizing, based on the flex item's content.
values.stretch: Sets the width of the element's [margin box](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Learn_web_development/Core/Styling_basics/Box_model#parts_of_a_box) to the width of its [containing block](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Guides/Display/Containing_block#identifying_the_containing_block). It attempts to make the margin box fill the available space in the containing block, so in a way behaving similar to `100%` but applying the resulting size to the margin box rather than the box determined by [box-sizing](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Reference/Properties/box-sizing).
values.fit-content: Use the fit-content inline size or fit-content block size, as appropriate to the writing mode.
values.max-content: Use the max-content inline size or max-content block size, as appropriate to the writing mode.
values.min-content: Use the min-content inline size or min-content block size, as appropriate to the writing mode.
values.cap: Equal to the "cap height" (nominal height of capital letters) of the element's `font`.
values.ch: Represents the width or, more precisely, the `advance measure` of the glyph `0` (zero, the Unicode character U+0030) in the element's `font`. In cases where determining the measure of the `0` glyph is impossible or impractical, it must be assumed to be `0.5em` wide by `1em` tall.
values.em: Represents the calculated `font-size` of the element. If used on the `font-size` property itself, it represents the _inherited_ font-size of the element.
values.ex: Equal to the [x-height](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/X-height) of the element's `font`. In fonts with the `x` letter, this is generally the height of lowercase letters in the font; `1ex ≈ 0.5em` in many fonts.
values.ic: Represents the used `advance measure` of the "水" glyph (CJK water ideograph, U+6C34), found in the font used to render it.
values.lh: Equal to the computed value of the `line-height` property of the element on which it is used, converted to an absolute length. This unit enables length calculations based on the theoretical size of an ideal empty line. However, the size of actual line boxes may differ based on their content.
values.rcap: Equal to the "cap height" (nominal height of capital letters) of the root element's `font`.
values.rch: Equal to the width or the `advance measure` of the glyph `0` (zero, the Unicode character U+0030) in the root element's `font`.
values.rem: Represents the `font-size` of the root element (typically `html`). When used within the root element `font-size`, it represents its initial value. A common browser default is `16px`, but user-defined preferences may modify this.
values.rex: Equal to the x-height of the root element's `font`.
values.ric: Equal to the value of [`ic`](#ic) unit on the root element's font.
values.rlh: Equal to the value of [`lh`](#lh) unit on the root element's font. This unit enables length calculations based on the theoretical size of an ideal empty line. However, the size of actual line boxes may differ based on their content.
values.vh: Represents a percentage of the height of the viewport's initial [containing block](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Guides/Display/Containing_block). `1vh` is 1% of the viewport height. For example, if the viewport height is `300px`, then a value of `70vh` on a property will be `210px`.
values.vw: Represents a percentage of the width of the viewport's initial [containing block](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Guides/Display/Containing_block). `1vw` is 1% of the viewport width. For example, if the viewport width is `800px`, then a value of `50vw` on a property will be `400px`.
values.vmax: Represents in percentage the largest of `vw` and `vh`.
values.vmin: Represents in percentage the smallest of `vw` and `vh`.
values.vb: Represents the percentage of the size of the initial [containing block](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Guides/Display/Containing_block), in the direction of the root element's [block axis](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Guides/Logical_properties_and_values).
values.vi: Represents a percentage of the size of the initial [containing block](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Guides/Display/Containing_block), in the direction of the root element's [inline axis](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Guides/Logical_properties_and_values).
values.cqw: Represents a percentage of the width of the query container. `1cqw` is 1% of the query container's width. For example, if the query container's width is `800px`, then a value of `50cqw` on a property will be `400px`.
values.cqh: Represents a percentage of the height of the query container. `1cqh` is 1% of the query container's height. For example, if the query container's height is `300px`, then a value of `10cqh` on a property will be `30px`.
values.cqi: Represents a percentage of the inline size of the query container. `1cqi` is 1% of the query container's inline size. For example, if the query container's inline size is `800px`, then a value of `50cqi` on a property will be `400px`.
values.cqb: Represents a percentage of the block size of the query container. `1cqb` is 1% of the query container's block size. For example, if the query container's block size is `300px`, then a value of `10cqb` on a property will be `30px`.
values.cqmin: Represents a percentage of the smaller value of either the query container's inline size or block size. `1cqmin` is 1% of the smaller value of either the query container's inline size or block size. For example, if the query container's inline size is `800px` and its block size is `300px`, then a value of `50cqmin` on a property will be `150px`.
values.cqmax: Represents a percentage of the larger value of either the query container's inline size or block size. `1cqmax` is 1% of the larger value of either the query container's inline size or block size. For example, if the query container's inline size is `800px` and its block size is `300px`, then a value of `50cqmax` on a property will be `400px`.
values.px: One pixel. For screen displays, it traditionally represents one `device pixel` (dot). However, for _printers_ and _high-resolution screens_, one CSS pixel implies multiple device pixels. `1px` = `1in / 96`.
values.height: The height of the anchor element.
values.block: The length of the anchor element's [containing block](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Guides/Display/Containing_block) in the block direction.
values.inline: The length of the anchor element's containing block in the inline direction.
values.self-block: The length of the anchor element in the block direction.
values.self-inline: The length of the anchor element in the inline direction.

flex-direction.description: The `flex-direction` [CSS](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS) property sets how flex items are placed in the flex container defining the main axis and the direction (normal or reversed).

values.row: Specifies the flex container's main-axis to be the same as the text direction. This is the default value.
values.row-reverse: Behaves the same as `row` but specifies the content direction to be inverted, with the first item placed at the inline-end edge.
values.column: Specifies the flex container's main-axis to be the same as the block-axis.
values.column-reverse: Behaves the same as `column` but specifies the content direction to be inverted, with the first item placed at the block-end edge.

flex-flow.description: The `flex-flow` [CSS](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS) [shorthand](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Guides/Cascade/Shorthand_properties) property specifies the direction of a flex container, as well as its wrapping behavior.

values.column: The flex container's main axis has the same orientation as the block axis of the current writing mode.
values.column-reverse: Same as 'column', except the main-start and main-end directions are swapped.
values.row: The flex container's main axis has the same orientation as the inline axis of the current writing mode.
values.row-reverse: Same as 'row', except the main-start and main-end directions are swapped.
values.wrap-reverse: Same as 'wrap', except the cross-start and cross-end directions are swapped.
values.balance: Specifies that flex items broken across multiple lines are distributed so that the line lengths are as similar as possible. If `balance` is specified as the only keyword, the other keyword defaults to `wrap`.

flex-grow.description: The `flex-grow` [CSS](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS) property sets the flex grow factor, which specifies how much of the flex container's [positive free space](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Guides/Flexible_box_layout/Controlling_flex_item_ratios), if any, should be assigned to the flex item's [main size](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Learn_web_development/Core/CSS_layout/Flexbox#the_flex_model).

flex-line-count.description: The `flex-line-count` [CSS](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS) property sets the minimum number of flex lines that flex items will be balanced over in cases where a flex container's `flex-wrap` or `flex-flow` property includes the `balance` keyword.

flex-shrink.description: The `flex-shrink` [CSS](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS) property sets the flex shrink factor of a flex item. If the size of all flex items is larger than the flex container, the [flex items can shrink](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Guides/Flexible_box_layout/Controlling_flex_item_ratios#the_flex-shrink_property) to fit according to their `flex-shrink` value. Each flex line's [negative free space](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Guides/Flexible_box_layout/Controlling_flex_item_ratios#positive_and_negative_free_space) is distributed between the line's flex items that have a `flex-shrink` value greater than `0`.

flex-wrap.description: The `flex-wrap` [CSS](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS) property sets whether flex items are forced onto one line or can wrap onto multiple lines. If wrapping is allowed, it sets the direction that lines are stacked.

values.nowrap: The flex items are laid out in a single line which may cause the flex container to overflow. This is the initial value.
values.wrap: The flex items can break into multiple lines.
values.wrap-reverse: Behaves the same as `wrap`, but with the lines laid out in reverse order.
values.balance: Specifies that flex items broken across multiple lines are distributed so that the line lengths are as similar as possible. If `balance` is specified as the only keyword, the other keyword defaults to `wrap`.

float.description: The `float` [CSS](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS) property places an element on the left or right side of its container, allowing text and inline elements to wrap around it. The element is removed from the normal flow of the page, though still remaining a part of the flow (in contrast to [absolute positioning](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Reference/Properties/position#absolute_positioning)).

values.left: The element must float on the left side of its containing block.
values.right: The element must float on the right side of its containing block.
values.none: The element must not float.
values.inline-start: The element must float on the start side of its containing block. That is the left side with `ltr` scripts, and the right side with `rtl` scripts.
values.inline-end: The element must float on the end side of its containing block. That is the right side with `ltr` scripts, and the left side with `rtl` scripts.

flood-color.description: The `flood-color` [CSS](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS) property defines the color of the current filter primitive subregion in `feFlood` and `feDropShadow` elements within a `filter`. If present, it overrides the element's `flood-color` attribute.

values.R: The _red_ component of the color, as a case-insensitive hexadecimal number between `0` and `ff` (255). If there is only one number, it is duplicated: `1` means `11`.
values.RR: The _red_ component of the color, as a case-insensitive hexadecimal number between `0` and `ff` (255). If there is only one number, it is duplicated: `1` means `11`.
values.G: The _green_ component of the color, as a case-insensitive hexadecimal number between `0` and `ff` (255). If there is only one number, it is duplicated: `c` means `cc`.
values.GG: The _green_ component of the color, as a case-insensitive hexadecimal number between `0` and `ff` (255). If there is only one number, it is duplicated: `c` means `cc`.
values.B: The _blue_ component of the color, as a case-insensitive hexadecimal number between `0` and `ff` (255). If there is only one number, it is duplicated: `9` means `99`.
values.BB: The _blue_ component of the color, as a case-insensitive hexadecimal number between `0` and `ff` (255). If there is only one number, it is duplicated: `9` means `99`.
values.A: The _alpha_ component of the color, indicating its transparency, as a case-insensitive hexadecimal number between `0` and `ff` (255). If there is only one number, it is duplicated: `e` means `ee`. `0`, or `00`, represents a fully transparent color, and `f`, or `ff`, a fully opaque one.
values.AA: The _alpha_ component of the color, indicating its transparency, as a case-insensitive hexadecimal number between `0` and `ff` (255). If there is only one number, it is duplicated: `e` means `ee`. `0`, or `00`, represents a fully transparent color, and `f`, or `ff`, a fully opaque one.

flood-opacity.description: The `flood-opacity` [CSS](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS) property defines the opacity of the current filter primitive subregion in `feFlood` and `feDropShadow` elements within a `filter`. If present, it overrides the element's `flood-opacity` attribute.

font.description: The `font` [CSS](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS) [shorthand](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Guides/Cascade/Shorthand_properties) property sets all the different properties of an element's font. Alternatively, it sets an element's font to a system font.

values.bolder: Specifies the weight of the face bolder than the inherited value.
values.caption: The font used for captioned controls (e.g., buttons, drop-downs, etc.).
values.icon: The font used to label icons.
values.italic: Selects a font that is labeled 'italic', or, if that is not available, one labeled 'oblique'.
values.lighter: Specifies the weight of the face lighter than the inherited value.
values.menu: The font used in menus (e.g., dropdown menus and menu lists).
values.message-box: The font used in dialog boxes.
values.normal: Specifies a face that is not labeled as a small-caps font.
values.oblique: Selects a font that is labeled 'oblique'.
values.small-caps: Specifies a font that is labeled as a small-caps font. If a genuine small-caps font is not available, user agents should simulate a small-caps font.
values.small-caption: The font used for labeling small controls.
values.status-bar: The font used in window status bars.
values.deg: Represents an angle in [degrees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Degree_%28angle%29). One full circle is `360deg`. Examples: `0deg`, `90deg`, `14.23deg`.
values.grad: Represents an angle in [gradians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gradian). One full circle is `400grad`. Examples: `0grad`, `100grad`, `38.8grad`.
values.rad: Represents an angle in [radians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radian). One full circle is 2π radians which approximates to `6.2832rad`. `1rad` is 180/π degrees. Examples: `0rad`, `1.0708rad`, `6.2832rad`.
values.turn: Represents an angle in a number of turns. One full circle is `1turn`. Examples: `0turn`, `0.25turn`, `1.2turn`.
values.xx-small: [Absolute-size](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Reference/Values/absolute-size) keywords, based on the user's default font size (which is `medium`).
values.x-small: [Absolute-size](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Reference/Values/absolute-size) keywords, based on the user's default font size (which is `medium`).
values.small: [Absolute-size](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Reference/Values/absolute-size) keywords, based on the user's default font size (which is `medium`).
values.medium: [Absolute-size](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Reference/Values/absolute-size) keywords, based on the user's default font size (which is `medium`).
values.large: [Absolute-size](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Reference/Values/absolute-size) keywords, based on the user's default font size (which is `medium`).
values.x-large: [Absolute-size](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Reference/Values/absolute-size) keywords, based on the user's default font size (which is `medium`).
values.xx-large: [Absolute-size](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Reference/Values/absolute-size) keywords, based on the user's default font size (which is `medium`).
values.xxx-large: [Absolute-size](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Reference/Values/absolute-size) keywords, based on the user's default font size (which is `medium`).
values.larger: [Relative-size](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Reference/Values/relative-size) keywords. The font will be larger or smaller relative to the parent element's font size, roughly by the ratio used to separate the absolute-size keywords above.
values.smaller: [Relative-size](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Reference/Values/relative-size) keywords. The font will be larger or smaller relative to the parent element's font size, roughly by the ratio used to separate the absolute-size keywords above.
values.math: [Scaling rules](https://w3c.github.io/mathml-core/#the-math-script-level-property) are applied when determining the computed value of the `font-size` property for math elements relative to the `font-size` of the containing parent. See the [math-depth](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Reference/Properties/math-depth) property for more information.
values.cap: Equal to the "cap height" (nominal height of capital letters) of the element's `font`.
values.ch: Represents the width or, more precisely, the `advance measure` of the glyph `0` (zero, the Unicode character U+0030) in the element's `font`. In cases where determining the measure of the `0` glyph is impossible or impractical, it must be assumed to be `0.5em` wide by `1em` tall.
values.em: Represents the calculated `font-size` of the element. If used on the `font-size` property itself, it represents the _inherited_ font-size of the element.
values.ex: Equal to the [x-height](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/X-height) of the element's `font`. In fonts with the `x` letter, this is generally the height of lowercase letters in the font; `1ex ≈ 0.5em` in many fonts.
values.ic: Represents the used `advance measure` of the "水" glyph (CJK water ideograph, U+6C34), found in the font used to render it.
values.lh: Equal to the computed value of the `line-height` property of the element on which it is used, converted to an absolute length. This unit enables length calculations based on the theoretical size of an ideal empty line. However, the size of actual line boxes may differ based on their content.
values.rcap: Equal to the "cap height" (nominal height of capital letters) of the root element's `font`.
values.rch: Equal to the width or the `advance measure` of the glyph `0` (zero, the Unicode character U+0030) in the root element's `font`.
values.rem: Represents the `font-size` of the root element (typically `html`). When used within the root element `font-size`, it represents its initial value. A common browser default is `16px`, but user-defined preferences may modify this.
values.rex: Equal to the x-height of the root element's `font`.
values.ric: Equal to the value of [`ic`](#ic) unit on the root element's font.
values.rlh: Equal to the value of [`lh`](#lh) unit on the root element's font. This unit enables length calculations based on the theoretical size of an ideal empty line. However, the size of actual line boxes may differ based on their content.
values.vh: Represents a percentage of the height of the viewport's initial [containing block](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Guides/Display/Containing_block). `1vh` is 1% of the viewport height. For example, if the viewport height is `300px`, then a value of `70vh` on a property will be `210px`.
values.vw: Represents a percentage of the width of the viewport's initial [containing block](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Guides/Display/Containing_block). `1vw` is 1% of the viewport width. For example, if the viewport width is `800px`, then a value of `50vw` on a property will be `400px`.
values.vmax: Represents in percentage the largest of `vw` and `vh`.
values.vmin: Represents in percentage the smallest of `vw` and `vh`.
values.vb: Represents the percentage of the size of the initial [containing block](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Guides/Display/Containing_block), in the direction of the root element's [block axis](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Guides/Logical_properties_and_values).
values.vi: Represents a percentage of the size of the initial [containing block](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Guides/Display/Containing_block), in the direction of the root element's [inline axis](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Guides/Logical_properties_and_values).
values.cqw: Represents a percentage of the width of the query container. `1cqw` is 1% of the query container's width. For example, if the query container's width is `800px`, then a value of `50cqw` on a property will be `400px`.
values.cqh: Represents a percentage of the height of the query container. `1cqh` is 1% of the query container's height. For example, if the query container's height is `300px`, then a value of `10cqh` on a property will be `30px`.
values.cqi: Represents a percentage of the inline size of the query container. `1cqi` is 1% of the query container's inline size. For example, if the query container's inline size is `800px`, then a value of `50cqi` on a property will be `400px`.
values.cqb: Represents a percentage of the block size of the query container. `1cqb` is 1% of the query container's block size. For example, if the query container's block size is `300px`, then a value of `10cqb` on a property will be `30px`.
values.cqmin: Represents a percentage of the smaller value of either the query container's inline size or block size. `1cqmin` is 1% of the smaller value of either the query container's inline size or block size. For example, if the query container's inline size is `800px` and its block size is `300px`, then a value of `50cqmin` on a property will be `150px`.
values.cqmax: Represents a percentage of the larger value of either the query container's inline size or block size. `1cqmax` is 1% of the larger value of either the query container's inline size or block size. For example, if the query container's inline size is `800px` and its block size is `300px`, then a value of `50cqmax` on a property will be `400px`.
values.px: One pixel. For screen displays, it traditionally represents one `device pixel` (dot). However, for _printers_ and _high-resolution screens_, one CSS pixel implies multiple device pixels. `1px` = `1in / 96`.
values.sans-serif: Glyphs have stroke endings that are plain.
values.monospace: All glyphs have the same fixed width.
values.cursive: Glyphs in cursive fonts generally have either joining strokes or other cursive characteristics beyond those of italic typefaces. The glyphs are partially or completely connected, and the result looks more like handwritten pen or brush writing than printed letter work.
values.fantasy: Fantasy fonts are primarily decorative fonts that contain playful representations of characters.
values.system-ui: Glyphs are taken from the default user interface font on a given platform. Because typographic traditions vary widely across the world, this generic is provided for typefaces that don't map cleanly into the other generics. > [!NOTE] > As the name implies, `system-ui` is intended to make UI elements look like native apps, and not for typesetting large paragraphs of text. It may cause the displayed typeface to be undesirable for some users—for example, the default Windows CJK font may render Latin scripts poorly, and the `lang` attribute may not affect the displayed font. Some operating systems do not allow customizing `system-ui`, while browsers generally allow customizing the `sans-serif` font family. For large paragraphs, use `sans-serif` or some other non-UI font family instead. - `ui-serif` - : The default user interface serif font. - `ui-sans-serif` - : The default user interface sans-serif font. - `ui-monospace` - : The default user interface monospace font. - `ui-rounded` - : The default user interface font that has rounded features. - `math` - : Font that addresses the particular stylistic concerns of representing mathematics: superscript and subscript, brackets that cross several lines, nesting expressions, and double struck glyphs with distinct meanings. UA stylesheets may set `math { font-family: math }` so that the element uses appropriate fonts by default. - `fangsong` - : A particular style of Chinese characters that are between serif-style Song and cursive-style Kai forms. This style is often used for government documents.
values.none: Sets the value of the `font-variant-ligatures` as `none` and the values of the other longhand properties as `normal`, their initial value.
values.historical-forms: Specifies the keywords and functions related to the `font-variant-ligatures` longhand property.
values.all-small-caps: Specifies the keywords and functions related to the `font-variant-caps` longhand property. The `small-caps` value is the only non-`normal` font variant valid within the `font` shorthand property.
values.petite-caps: Specifies the keywords and functions related to the `font-variant-caps` longhand property. The `small-caps` value is the only non-`normal` font variant valid within the `font` shorthand property.
values.all-petite-caps: Specifies the keywords and functions related to the `font-variant-caps` longhand property. The `small-caps` value is the only non-`normal` font variant valid within the `font` shorthand property.
values.unicase: Specifies the keywords and functions related to the `font-variant-caps` longhand property. The `small-caps` value is the only non-`normal` font variant valid within the `font` shorthand property.
values.titling-caps: Specifies the keywords and functions related to the `font-variant-caps` longhand property. The `small-caps` value is the only non-`normal` font variant valid within the `font` shorthand property.
values.ordinal: Specifies the keywords related to the `font-variant-numeric` longhand property. The possible values are `lining-nums`, `oldstyle-nums`, `proportional-nums`, `tabular-nums`, `diagonal-fractions`, `stacked-fractions`, `ordinal`, and `slashed-zero`.
values.slashed-zero: Specifies the keywords related to the `font-variant-numeric` longhand property. The possible values are `lining-nums`, `oldstyle-nums`, `proportional-nums`, `tabular-nums`, `diagonal-fractions`, `stacked-fractions`, `ordinal`, and `slashed-zero`.
values.ruby: Specifies the keywords related to the `font-variant-east-asian` longhand property. The possible values are `jis78`, `jis83`, `jis90`, `jis04`, `simplified`, `traditional`, `full-width`, `proportional-width`, and `ruby`.
values.sub: Specifies the keywords and functions related to the `font-variant-position` longhand property.
values.super: Specifies the keywords and functions related to the `font-variant-position` longhand property.
values.text: Specifies the keywords and functions related to the `font-variant-emoji` longhand property.
values.emoji: Specifies the keywords and functions related to the `font-variant-emoji` longhand property.
values.unicode: Specifies the keywords and functions related to the `font-variant-emoji` longhand property.
values.semi-condensed: Specifies a more condensed font face than normal, with `ultra-condensed` being the most condensed.
values.condensed: Specifies a more condensed font face than normal, with `ultra-condensed` being the most condensed.
values.extra-condensed: Specifies a more condensed font face than normal, with `ultra-condensed` being the most condensed.
values.ultra-condensed: Specifies a more condensed font face than normal, with `ultra-condensed` being the most condensed.
values.semi-expanded: Specifies a more expanded font face than normal, with `ultra-expanded` being the most expanded.
values.expanded: Specifies a more expanded font face than normal, with `ultra-expanded` being the most expanded.
values.extra-expanded: Specifies a more expanded font face than normal, with `ultra-expanded` being the most expanded.
values.ultra-expanded: Specifies a more expanded font face than normal, with `ultra-expanded` being the most expanded.
values.narrower: Indicates a narrower value relative to the width of the parent element.
values.wider: Indicates a wider value relative to the width of the parent element.

values.normal: Indicates that text is laid out using default font settings. This is the default value.
values.\"abvf\": Above-base Forms. Required in Khmer script.
values.\"abvm\": Above-base Mark Positioning. Required in Indic scripts.
values.\"abvs\": Above-base Substitutions. Required in Indic scripts.
values.\"akhn\": Akhand. Required in most Indic scripts.
values.\"blwf\": Below-base Form. Required in a number of Indic scripts.
values.\"blwm\": Below-base Mark Positioning. Required in Indic scripts.
values.\"blws\": Below-base Substitutions. Required in Indic scripts.
values.\"case\": Case-Sensitive Forms. Applies only to European scripts; particularly prominent in Spanish-language setting.
values.\"cfar\": Conjunct Form After Ro. Required in Khmer scripts.
values.\"cjct\": Conjunct Forms. Required in Indic scripts that show similarity to Devanagari.
values.\"cpct\": Centered CJK Punctuation. Used primarily in Chinese fonts.
values.\"cpsp\": Capital Spacing. Should not be used in connecting scripts (e.g. most Arabic).
values.\"curs\": Cursive Positioning. Can be used in any cursive script.
values.\"c2pc\": Petite Capitals From Capitals. Applies only to bicameral scripts.
values.\"c2sc\": Small Capitals From Capitals. Applies only to bicameral scripts.
values.\"dtls\": Dotless Forms. Applied to math formula layout.
values.\"expt\": Expert Forms. Applies only to Japanese.
values.\"falt\": Final Glyph on Line Alternates. Can be used in any cursive script.
values.\"fin2\": Terminal Form #2. Used only with the Syriac script.
values.\"fin3\": Terminal Form #3. Used only with the Syriac script.
values.\"fina\": Terminal Forms. Can be used in any alphabetic script.
values.\"flac\": Flattened ascent forms. Applied to math formula layout.
values.\"fwid\": Full Widths. Applies to any script which can use monospaced forms.
values.\"half\": Half Forms. Required in Indic scripts that show similarity to Devanagari.
values.\"haln\": Halant Forms. Required in Indic scripts.
values.\"halt\": Alternate Half Widths. Used only in CJKV fonts.
values.\"hkna\": Horizontal Kana Alternates. Applies only to fonts that support kana (hiragana and katakana).
values.\"hojo\": Hojo Kanji Forms (JIS X 0212-1990 Kanji Forms). Used only with Kanji script.
values.\"hwid\": Half Widths. Generally used only in CJKV fonts.
values.\"init\": Initial Forms. Can be used in any alphabetic script.
values.\"isol\": Isolated Forms. Can be used in any cursive script.
values.\"ital\": Italics. Applies mostly to Latin; note that many non-Latin fonts contain Latin as well.
values.\"jalt\": Justification Alternates. Can be used in any cursive script.
values.\"jp78\": JIS78 Forms. Applies only to Japanese.
values.\"jp83\": JIS83 Forms. Applies only to Japanese.
values.\"jp90\": JIS90 Forms. Applies only to Japanese.
values.\"jp04\": JIS2004 Forms. Applies only to Japanese.
values.\"ljmo\": Leading Jamo Forms. Required for Hangul script when Ancient Hangul writing system is supported.
values.\"med2\": Medial Form #2. Used only with the Syriac script.
values.\"nlck\": NLC Kanji Forms. Used only with Kanji script.
values.\"nukt\": Nukta Forms. Required in Indic scripts..
values.\"ordn\": Ordinals. Applies mostly to Latin script.
values.\"palt\": Proportional Alternate Widths. Used mostly in CJKV fonts.
values.\"pkna\": Proportional Kana. Generally used only in Japanese fonts.
values.\"pref\": Pre-base Forms. Required in Khmer and Myanmar (Burmese) scripts and southern Indic scripts that may display a pre-base form of Ra.
values.\"pres\": Pre-base Substitutions. Required in Indic scripts.
values.\"pstf\": Post-base Forms. Required in scripts of south and southeast Asia that have post-base forms for consonants eg: Gurmukhi, Malayalam, Khmer.
values.\"qwid\": Quarter Widths. Generally used only in CJKV fonts.
values.\"rclt\": Required Contextual Alternates. May apply to any script, but is especially important for many styles of Arabic.
values.\"rlig\": Required Ligatures. Applies to Arabic and Syriac. May apply to some other scripts.
values.\"rkrf\": Rakar Forms. Required in Devanagari and Gujarati scripts.
values.\"rphf\": Reph Form. Required in Indic scripts. E.g. Devanagari, Kannada.
values.\"ruby\": Ruby Notation Forms. Applies only to Japanese.
values.\"smcp\": Small Capitals. Applies only to bicameral scripts.
values.\"smpl\": Simplified Forms. Applies only to Chinese and Japanese.
values.\"swsh\": Swash. Does not apply to ideographic scripts.
values.\"tjmo\": Trailing Jamo Forms. Required for Hangul script when Ancient Hangul writing system is supported.
values.\"tnam\": Traditional Name Forms. Applies only to Japanese.
values.\"trad\": Traditional Forms. Applies only to Chinese and Japanese.
values.\"twid\": Third Widths. Generally used only in CJKV fonts.
values.\"valt\": Alternate Vertical Metrics. Applies only to scripts with vertical writing modes.
values.\"vatu\": Vattu Variants. Used for Indic scripts. E.g. Devanagari.
values.\"vert\": Vertical Alternates. Applies only to scripts with vertical writing modes.
values.\"vhal\": Alternate Vertical Half Metrics. Used only in CJKV fonts.
values.\"vjmo\": Vowel Jamo Forms. Required for Hangul script when Ancient Hangul writing system is supported.
values.\"vkna\": Vertical Kana Alternates. Applies only to fonts that support kana (hiragana and katakana).
values.\"vpal\": Proportional Alternate Vertical Metrics. Used mostly in CJKV fonts.
values.\"vrt2\": Vertical Alternates and Rotation. Applies only to scripts with vertical writing modes.

font-kerning.description: The `font-kerning` [CSS](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS) property sets the use of the kerning information stored in a font.

values.auto: The browser determines whether font kerning should be used or not. For example, some browsers will disable kerning on small fonts, since applying it could harm the readability of text.
values.normal: Font kerning information stored in the font must be applied.
values.none: Font kerning information stored in the font is disabled.

font-language-override.description: The `font-language-override` [CSS](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS) property controls the use of language-specific glyphs in a typeface.

values.normal: Tells the browser to use font glyphs that are appropriate for the language specified by the `lang` attribute. This is the default value.

font-optical-sizing.description: The `font-optical-sizing` [CSS](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS) property sets whether text rendering is optimized for viewing at different sizes.

values.none: The browser will not modify the shape of glyphs for optimal viewing.
values.auto: The browser will modify the shape of glyphs for optimal viewing.

font-palette.description: The `font-palette` [CSS](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS) property allows specifying one of the many palettes contained in a [color font](https://www.colorfonts.wtf/) that a user agent may use for the font. Users can also override the values in a palette or create a new palette by using the `@font-palette-values` at-rule.

values.normal: Specifies the default color palette or the default glyph colorization (set by the font maker) to be used for the font. With this setting, the palette in the font at index 0 is rendered.
values.light: Specifies the first palette in the font that matches 'light' to be used for the font. Some fonts contain metadata that identify a palette as applicable for a light (close to white) background. If a font does not have this metadata, the `light` value behaves as `normal`.
values.dark: Specifies the first palette in the font that matches 'dark' to be used for the font. Some fonts contain metadata that identify a palette as applicable for a dark (close to black) background. If a font does not have this metadata, the value behaves as `normal`.

font-size.description: The `font-size` [CSS](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS) property sets the size of the font. Changing the font size also updates the sizes of the font size-relative `<length>` units, such as `em`, `ex`, and so forth.
