values.em: Represents the calculated `font-size` of the element. If used on the `font-size` property itself, it represents the _inherited_ font-size of the element.
values.ex: Equal to the [x-height](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/X-height) of the element's `font`. In fonts with the `x` letter, this is generally the height of lowercase letters in the font; `1ex ≈ 0.5em` in many fonts.
values.ic: Represents the used `advance measure` of the "水" glyph (CJK water ideograph, U+6C34), found in the font used to render it.
values.lh: Equal to the computed value of the `line-height` property of the element on which it is used, converted to an absolute length. This unit enables length calculations based on the theoretical size of an ideal empty line. However, the size of actual line boxes may differ based on their content.
values.rcap: Equal to the "cap height" (nominal height of capital letters) of the root element's `font`.
values.rch: Equal to the width or the `advance measure` of the glyph `0` (zero, the Unicode character U+0030) in the root element's `font`.
values.rem: Represents the `font-size` of the root element (typically `html`). When used within the root element `font-size`, it represents its initial value. A common browser default is `16px`, but user-defined preferences may modify this.
values.rex: Equal to the x-height of the root element's `font`.
values.ric: Equal to the value of [`ic`](#ic) unit on the root element's font.
values.rlh: Equal to the value of [`lh`](#lh) unit on the root element's font. This unit enables length calculations based on the theoretical size of an ideal empty line. However, the size of actual line boxes may differ based on their content.
values.vh: Represents a percentage of the height of the viewport's initial [containing block](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Guides/Display/Containing_block). `1vh` is 1% of the viewport height. For example, if the viewport height is `300px`, then a value of `70vh` on a property will be `210px`.
values.vw: Represents a percentage of the width of the viewport's initial [containing block](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Guides/Display/Containing_block). `1vw` is 1% of the viewport width. For example, if the viewport width is `800px`, then a value of `50vw` on a property will be `400px`.
values.vmax: Represents in percentage the largest of `vw` and `vh`.
values.vmin: Represents in percentage the smallest of `vw` and `vh`.
values.vb: Represents the percentage of the size of the initial [containing block](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Guides/Display/Containing_block), in the direction of the root element's [block axis](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Guides/Logical_properties_and_values).
values.vi: Represents a percentage of the size of the initial [containing block](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Guides/Display/Containing_block), in the direction of the root element's [inline axis](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Guides/Logical_properties_and_values).
values.cqw: Represents a percentage of the width of the query container. `1cqw` is 1% of the query container's width. For example, if the query container's width is `800px`, then a value of `50cqw` on a property will be `400px`.
values.cqh: Represents a percentage of the height of the query container. `1cqh` is 1% of the query container's height. For example, if the query container's height is `300px`, then a value of `10cqh` on a property will be `30px`.
values.cqi: Represents a percentage of the inline size of the query container. `1cqi` is 1% of the query container's inline size. For example, if the query container's inline size is `800px`, then a value of `50cqi` on a property will be `400px`.
values.cqb: Represents a percentage of the block size of the query container. `1cqb` is 1% of the query container's block size. For example, if the query container's block size is `300px`, then a value of `10cqb` on a property will be `30px`.
values.cqmin: Represents a percentage of the smaller value of either the query container's inline size or block size. `1cqmin` is 1% of the smaller value of either the query container's inline size or block size. For example, if the query container's inline size is `800px` and its block size is `300px`, then a value of `50cqmin` on a property will be `150px`.
values.cqmax: Represents a percentage of the larger value of either the query container's inline size or block size. `1cqmax` is 1% of the larger value of either the query container's inline size or block size. For example, if the query container's inline size is `800px` and its block size is `300px`, then a value of `50cqmax` on a property will be `400px`.
values.px: One pixel. For screen displays, it traditionally represents one `device pixel` (dot). However, for _printers_ and _high-resolution screens_, one CSS pixel implies multiple device pixels. `1px` = `1in / 96`.

font-size-adjust.description: The `font-size-adjust` [CSS](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS) property adjusts the size of a font to match a chosen font metric, such as the height of lowercase letters, to a specified proportion of the `font-size`. This property is intended for adjusting fallback fonts to have similar metrics as the first-choice font.

values.none: No font size adjustment is applied.
values.from-font: Uses the `<number>` value for the specified `<font-metric>` from the first available font.

font-stretch.description: The `font-stretch` [CSS](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS) property selects a normal, condensed, or expanded face from a font.

values.normal: Specifies a normally condensed font face.
values.semi-condensed: Specifies a more condensed font face than normal, with `ultra-condensed` being the most condensed.
values.condensed: Specifies a more condensed font face than normal, with `ultra-condensed` being the most condensed.
values.extra-condensed: Specifies a more condensed font face than normal, with `ultra-condensed` being the most condensed.
values.ultra-condensed: Specifies a more condensed font face than normal, with `ultra-condensed` being the most condensed.
values.semi-expanded: Specifies a more expanded font face than normal, with `ultra-expanded` being the most expanded.
values.expanded: Specifies a more expanded font face than normal, with `ultra-expanded` being the most expanded.
values.extra-expanded: Specifies a more expanded font face than normal, with `ultra-expanded` being the most expanded.
values.ultra-expanded: Specifies a more expanded font face than normal, with `ultra-expanded` being the most expanded.
values.narrower: Indicates a narrower value relative to the width of the parent element.
values.wider: Indicates a wider value relative to the width of the parent element.

font-style.description: The `font-style` [CSS](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS) property sets whether a font should be styled with a normal, italic, or oblique face from its `font-family`.

values.normal: Selects a font that is classified as `normal` within a `font-family`.
values.italic: Selects a font that is classified as `italic`. If no italic version of the face is available, one classified as `oblique` is used instead. If neither is available, the style is artificially simulated.
values.oblique: Selects a font classified as `oblique`, and additionally specifies an angle for the slant of the text. If one or more oblique faces are available in the chosen font family, the one that most closely matches the specified angle is chosen. If no oblique faces are available, the browser will synthesize an oblique version of the font by slanting a normal face by the specified amount. Valid values are degree values of `-90deg` to `90deg` inclusive. If an angle is not specified, an angle of 14 degrees is used. Positive values are slanted to the end of the line, while negative values are slanted towards the beginning.
values.deg: Represents an angle in [degrees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Degree_%28angle%29). One full circle is `360deg`. Examples: `0deg`, `90deg`, `14.23deg`.
values.grad: Represents an angle in [gradians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gradian). One full circle is `400grad`. Examples: `0grad`, `100grad`, `38.8grad`.
values.rad: Represents an angle in [radians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radian). One full circle is 2π radians which approximates to `6.2832rad`. `1rad` is 180/π degrees. Examples: `0rad`, `1.0708rad`, `6.2832rad`.
values.turn: Represents an angle in a number of turns. One full circle is `1turn`. Examples: `0turn`, `0.25turn`, `1.2turn`.

font-synthesis.description: The `font-synthesis` [CSS](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS) [shorthand](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Guides/Cascade/Shorthand_properties) property lets you specify whether or not the browser may synthesize the bold, italic, small-caps, and/or subscript and superscript typefaces when they are missing in the specified font-family.

values.none: Indicates that no bold, italic, or small-caps typeface may be synthesized by the browser.
values.weight: Indicates that the missing bold typeface may be synthesized by the browser if needed.
values.style: Indicates that the italic typeface may be synthesized by the browser if needed.
values.small-caps: Indicates that the small-caps typeface may be synthesized by the browser if needed.
values.position: Indicates that the subscript and superscript typeface may be synthesized by the browser, if needed, when using `font-variant-position`.

font-synthesis-position.description: The `font-synthesis-position` [CSS](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS) property lets you specify whether or not a browser may synthesize the subscript and superscript "position" typefaces when they are missing in a font family, while using `font-variant-position` to set the positions.

values.auto: Indicates that a missing position typeface may be synthesized by the browser if needed.
values.none: Indicates that the synthesis of a missing position typeface by the browser is not allowed.

font-synthesis-small-caps.description: The `font-synthesis-small-caps` [CSS](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS) property lets you specify whether or not the browser may synthesize small-caps typeface when it is missing in a font family. Small-caps glyphs typically use the form of uppercase letters but are reduced to the size of lowercase letters.

values.auto: Indicates that the missing small-caps typeface may be synthesized by the browser if needed.
values.none: Indicates that the synthesis of the missing small-caps typeface by the browser is not allowed.

font-synthesis-style.description: The `font-synthesis-style` [CSS](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS) property lets you specify whether or not the browser may synthesize the oblique typeface when it is missing in a font family.

values.auto: Indicates that the missing oblique typeface may be synthesized by the browser if needed.
values.none: Indicates that the synthesis of the missing oblique typeface by the browser is _not_ allowed.
values.oblique-only: Same as `auto`, but no font synthesis occurs if `font-style: italic` is set.

font-synthesis-weight.description: The `font-synthesis-weight` [CSS](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS) property lets you specify whether or not the browser may synthesize the bold typeface when it is missing in a font family.

values.auto: Indicates that the missing bold typeface may be synthesized by the browser if needed.
values.none: Indicates that the synthesis of the missing bold typeface by the browser is not allowed.

font-variant.description: The `font-variant` [CSS](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS) [shorthand](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Guides/Cascade/Shorthand_properties) property allows you to set all the font variants for a font.

values.normal: Specifies a normal font face. Each longhand property has an initial value of `normal`.
values.none: Sets the value of the `font-variant-ligatures` as `none` and the values of the other longhand properties as `normal`, their initial value.
values.historical-forms: Specifies the keywords and functions related to the `font-variant-ligatures` longhand property.
values.small-caps: Specifies the keywords and functions related to the `font-variant-caps` longhand property. The `small-caps` value is the only non-`normal` font variant valid within the `font` shorthand property.
values.all-small-caps: Specifies the keywords and functions related to the `font-variant-caps` longhand property. The `small-caps` value is the only non-`normal` font variant valid within the `font` shorthand property.
values.petite-caps: Specifies the keywords and functions related to the `font-variant-caps` longhand property. The `small-caps` value is the only non-`normal` font variant valid within the `font` shorthand property.
values.all-petite-caps: Specifies the keywords and functions related to the `font-variant-caps` longhand property. The `small-caps` value is the only non-`normal` font variant valid within the `font` shorthand property.
values.unicase: Specifies the keywords and functions related to the `font-variant-caps` longhand property. The `small-caps` value is the only non-`normal` font variant valid within the `font` shorthand property.
values.titling-caps: Specifies the keywords and functions related to the `font-variant-caps` longhand property. The `small-caps` value is the only non-`normal` font variant valid within the `font` shorthand property.
values.ordinal: Specifies the keywords related to the `font-variant-numeric` longhand property. The possible values are `lining-nums`, `oldstyle-nums`, `proportional-nums`, `tabular-nums`, `diagonal-fractions`, `stacked-fractions`, `ordinal`, and `slashed-zero`.
values.slashed-zero: Specifies the keywords related to the `font-variant-numeric` longhand property. The possible values are `lining-nums`, `oldstyle-nums`, `proportional-nums`, `tabular-nums`, `diagonal-fractions`, `stacked-fractions`, `ordinal`, and `slashed-zero`.
values.ruby: Specifies the keywords related to the `font-variant-east-asian` longhand property. The possible values are `jis78`, `jis83`, `jis90`, `jis04`, `simplified`, `traditional`, `full-width`, `proportional-width`, and `ruby`.
values.sub: Specifies the keywords and functions related to the `font-variant-position` longhand property.
values.super: Specifies the keywords and functions related to the `font-variant-position` longhand property.
values.text: Specifies the keywords and functions related to the `font-variant-emoji` longhand property.
values.emoji: Specifies the keywords and functions related to the `font-variant-emoji` longhand property.
values.unicode: Specifies the keywords and functions related to the `font-variant-emoji` longhand property.

font-variant-alternates.description: The `font-variant-alternates` [CSS](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS) property controls the usage of alternate glyphs. These alternate glyphs may be referenced by alternative names defined in `@font-feature-values`.

values.normal: This keyword deactivates alternate glyphs.
values.historical-forms: This keyword enables historical forms — glyphs that were common in the past but not today. It corresponds to the OpenType value `hist`.
values.annotation(): Enables display of alternate annotation forms.
values.character-variant(): Enables display of specific character variants.
values.ornaments(): Enables replacement of default glyphs with ornaments, if provided in the font.

font-variant-caps.description: The `font-variant-caps` [CSS](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS) property controls the use of alternate glyphs used for small or petite capitals or for titling.

values.normal: Deactivates of the use of alternate glyphs.
values.small-caps: Enables display of small capitals (OpenType feature: `smcp`). Small-caps glyphs typically use the form of uppercase letters but are displayed using the same size as lowercase letters.
values.all-small-caps: Enables display of small capitals for both upper and lowercase letters (OpenType features: `c2sc`, `smcp`).
values.petite-caps: Enables display of petite capitals (OpenType feature: `pcap`).
values.all-petite-caps: Enables display of petite capitals for both upper and lowercase letters (OpenType features: `c2pc`, `pcap`).
values.unicase: Enables display of mixture of small capitals for uppercase letters with normal lowercase letters (OpenType feature: `unic`).
values.titling-caps: Enables display of titling capitals (OpenType feature: `titl`). Uppercase letter glyphs are often designed for use with lowercase letters. When used in all uppercase titling sequences they can appear too strong. Titling capitals are designed specifically for this situation.

font-variant-east-asian.description: The `font-variant-east-asian` [CSS](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS) property controls the use of alternate glyphs for East Asian scripts, like Japanese and Chinese.

values.normal: This keyword leads to the deactivation of the use of such alternate glyphs.
values.ruby: This keyword forces the use of special glyphs for ruby characters. As these are usually smaller, font creators often designs specific forms, usually slightly bolder to improve the contrast. This keyword corresponds to the OpenType values `ruby`.

font-variant-emoji.description: The `font-variant-emoji` [CSS](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS) property specifies the default presentation style for displaying emojis.

values.normal: Allows a browser to choose how to display the emoji. This often follows the operating system setting.
values.text: Renders the emoji as if it were using the unicode text variation selector (`U+FE0E`).
values.emoji: Renders the emoji as if it were using the unicode emoji variation selector (`U+FE0F`).
values.unicode: Renders the emoji in accordance with the [Emoji presentation properties](https://www.unicode.org/reports/tr51/tr51-23.html#Emoji_Presentation). If the `U+FE0E` or `U+FE0F` variation selector is present, then it will override this value setting.

font-variant-ligatures.description: The `font-variant-ligatures` [CSS](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS) property controls which `ligatures` and contextual forms are used in the textual content of the elements it applies to. This leads to more harmonized forms in the resulting text.

values.normal: This keyword activates the usual ligatures and contextual forms needed for correct rendering. The ligatures and forms activated depend on the font, language, and kind of script. This is the default value.
values.none: This keyword specifies that all ligatures and contextual forms are disabled, even common ones.

font-variant-numeric.description: The `font-variant-numeric` [CSS](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS) property controls the usage of alternate glyphs for numbers, fractions, and ordinal markers.

values.normal: This keyword leads to the deactivation of the use of such alternate glyphs.
values.ordinal: This keyword forces the use of special glyphs for the ordinal markers, like 1st, 2nd, 3rd, 4th in English or a 1a in Italian. It corresponds to the OpenType values `ordn`.
values.slashed-zero: This keyword forces the use of a 0 with a slash; this is useful when a clear distinction between O and 0 is needed. It corresponds to the OpenType values `zero`.
values.diagonal-fractions: Enables display of lining diagonal fractions.
values.stacked-fractions: Enables display of lining stacked fractions.

font-variant-position.description: The `font-variant-position` [CSS](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS) property controls the use of alternate, smaller glyphs that are positioned as superscript or subscript.

values.normal: Deactivates alternate superscript and subscript glyphs.
values.sub: Activates subscript alternate glyphs. If, in a given run, one such glyph is not available for a character, all the characters in the run are rendered using synthesized glyphs.
values.super: Activates superscript alternate glyphs. If, in a given run, one such glyph is not available for a character, all the characters in the run are rendered using synthesized glyphs.

font-variation-settings.description: The `font-variation-settings` [CSS](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS) property provides low-level control over [variable font](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Guides/Fonts/Variable_fonts) characteristics by letting you specify the four letter axis names of the characteristics you want to vary along with their values.

values.normal: Text is laid out using default settings.

font-weight.description: The `font-weight` [CSS](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS) property sets the weight (or boldness) of the font. The weights available depend on the `font-family` that is currently set.

values.normal: Normal font weight. Same as `400`.
values.lighter: One relative font weight lighter than the parent element. Note that only four font weights are considered for relative weight calculation; see the [Meaning of relative weights](#meaning_of_relative_weights) section below.
values.bolder: One relative font weight heavier than the parent element. Note that only four font weights are considered for relative weight calculation; see the [Meaning of relative weights](#meaning_of_relative_weights) section below.

font-width.description: The `font-width` [CSS](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS) property selects a normal, condensed, or expanded face from a font.

values.normal: Specifies a normally condensed font face.
values.semi-condensed: Specifies a more condensed font face than normal, with `ultra-condensed` being the most condensed.
values.condensed: Specifies a more condensed font face than normal, with `ultra-condensed` being the most condensed.
values.extra-condensed: Specifies a more condensed font face than normal, with `ultra-condensed` being the most condensed.
values.ultra-condensed: Specifies a more condensed font face than normal, with `ultra-condensed` being the most condensed.
values.semi-expanded: Specifies a more expanded font face than normal, with `ultra-expanded` being the most expanded.
values.expanded: Specifies a more expanded font face than normal, with `ultra-expanded` being the most expanded.
values.extra-expanded: Specifies a more expanded font face than normal, with `ultra-expanded` being the most expanded.
values.ultra-expanded: Specifies a more expanded font face than normal, with `ultra-expanded` being the most expanded.

forced-color-adjust.description: The `forced-color-adjust` [CSS](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS) property allows authors to opt certain elements out of forced colors mode. This then restores the control of those values to CSS.

values.auto: The element's colors are adjusted by the `user agent` in forced colors mode. This is the default value.
values.none: The element's colors are not automatically adjusted by the `user agent` in forced colors mode.
values.preserve-parent-color: In forced colors mode, if the `color` property inherits from its parent (i.e., there is no [cascaded value](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Guides/Cascade/Introduction) or the cascaded value is `currentColor`, `inherit`, or another keyword that inherits from the parent), then it computes to the [used color](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Guides/Cascade/Property_value_processing#used_value) of its parent's `color` property. In all other cases, it behaves the same as `none`.

frame-sizing.description: The `frame-sizing` [CSS](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS) property can be used to set an `iframe` element's horizontal or vertical size to equal the layout size of its embedded document in the same dimension, but only if the embedded document has opted in to sharing its size information.

values.auto: The initial value. The `<iframe>` element's size is not affected by the layout size of its embedded document.
values.content-width: The `<iframe>` element's `width` is set to the layout width of its embedded document.
values.content-height: The `<iframe>` element's `height` is set to the layout height of its embedded document.
values.content-inline-size: The `<iframe>` element's `inline-size` is set to the layout size of its embedded document in the inline direction.
values.content-block-size: The `<iframe>` element's `block-size` is set to the layout size of its embedded document in the block direction.

gap.description: The `gap` [CSS](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS) [shorthand](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Guides/Cascade/Shorthand_properties) property sets the gaps (also called `gutters`) between rows and columns on [multi-column](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Guides/Multicol_layout), [flex](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Guides/Flexible_box_layout), and [grid](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Guides/Grid_layout) containers.

values.normal: Sets the gap to `1em` in multi-column layouts and to `0` in all other contexts. This is the default value.
values.cap: Equal to the "cap height" (nominal height of capital letters) of the element's `font`.
values.ch: Represents the width or, more precisely, the `advance measure` of the glyph `0` (zero, the Unicode character U+0030) in the element's `font`. In cases where determining the measure of the `0` glyph is impossible or impractical, it must be assumed to be `0.5em` wide by `1em` tall.
values.em: Represents the calculated `font-size` of the element. If used on the `font-size` property itself, it represents the _inherited_ font-size of the element.
values.ex: Equal to the [x-height](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/X-height) of the element's `font`. In fonts with the `x` letter, this is generally the height of lowercase letters in the font; `1ex ≈ 0.5em` in many fonts.
values.ic: Represents the used `advance measure` of the "水" glyph (CJK water ideograph, U+6C34), found in the font used to render it.
values.lh: Equal to the computed value of the `line-height` property of the element on which it is used, converted to an absolute length. This unit enables length calculations based on the theoretical size of an ideal empty line. However, the size of actual line boxes may differ based on their content.
values.rcap: Equal to the "cap height" (nominal height of capital letters) of the root element's `font`.
values.rch: Equal to the width or the `advance measure` of the glyph `0` (zero, the Unicode character U+0030) in the root element's `font`.
values.rem: Represents the `font-size` of the root element (typically `html`). When used within the root element `font-size`, it represents its initial value. A common browser default is `16px`, but user-defined preferences may modify this.
values.rex: Equal to the x-height of the root element's `font`.
values.ric: Equal to the value of [`ic`](#ic) unit on the root element's font.
values.rlh: Equal to the value of [`lh`](#lh) unit on the root element's font. This unit enables length calculations based on the theoretical size of an ideal empty line. However, the size of actual line boxes may differ based on their content.
values.vh: Represents a percentage of the height of the viewport's initial [containing block](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Guides/Display/Containing_block). `1vh` is 1% of the viewport height. For example, if the viewport height is `300px`, then a value of `70vh` on a property will be `210px`.
values.vw: Represents a percentage of the width of the viewport's initial [containing block](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Guides/Display/Containing_block). `1vw` is 1% of the viewport width. For example, if the viewport width is `800px`, then a value of `50vw` on a property will be `400px`.
values.vmax: Represents in percentage the largest of `vw` and `vh`.
values.vmin: Represents in percentage the smallest of `vw` and `vh`.
values.vb: Represents the percentage of the size of the initial [containing block](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Guides/Display/Containing_block), in the direction of the root element's [block axis](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Guides/Logical_properties_and_values).
values.vi: Represents a percentage of the size of the initial [containing block](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Guides/Display/Containing_block), in the direction of the root element's [inline axis](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Guides/Logical_properties_and_values).
values.cqw: Represents a percentage of the width of the query container. `1cqw` is 1% of the query container's width. For example, if the query container's width is `800px`, then a value of `50cqw` on a property will be `400px`.

hanging-punctuation.description: The `hanging-punctuation` [CSS](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS) property specifies whether a punctuation mark should hang at the start or end of a line of text. Hanging punctuation may be placed outside the line box.

values.none: No character hangs.
values.first: An opening bracket or quote at the start of the first formatted line of an element hangs. This applies to: - all characters in the Unicode categories [Ps](https://unicodeplus.com/category/Ps), [Pf](https://unicodeplus.com/category/Pf), [Pi](https://unicodeplus.com/category/Pi) - the quote marks `U+0027` APOSTROPHE (`'`) and `U+0022` QUOTATION MARK (`"`).
values.last: A closing bracket or quote at the end of the last formatted line of an element hangs. This applies to: - all characters in the Unicode categories [Pe](https://unicodeplus.com/category/Pe), [Pf](https://unicodeplus.com/category/Pf), [Pi](https://unicodeplus.com/category/Pi) - the quote marks `U+0027` APOSTROPHE (`'`) and `U+0022` QUOTATION MARK (`"`).
values.allow-end: A stop or comma at the end of a line hangs if it does not otherwise fit prior to justification.

height.description: The `height` [CSS](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS) property specifies the height of an element. By default, the property defines the height of the [content area](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Guides/Box_model/Introduction#content_area). If `box-sizing` is set to `border-box`, however, it instead determines the height of the [border area](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Guides/Box_model/Introduction#border_area).

values.auto: The browser will calculate and select a height for the specified element.
values.stretch: Sets the height of the element's [margin box](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Learn_web_development/Core/Styling_basics/Box_model#parts_of_a_box) to the height of its [containing block](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Guides/Display/Containing_block#identifying_the_containing_block). It attempts to make the margin box fill the available space in the containing block, so in a way behaving similar to `100%` but applying the resulting size to the margin box rather than the box determined by [box-sizing](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Reference/Properties/box-sizing).

values.max-content: Use the max-content inline size or max-content block size, as appropriate to the writing mode.

hyphenate-character.description: The `hyphenate-character` [CSS](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS) property sets the character (or string) used at the end of a line before a hyphenation break.

values.auto: The user-agent selects an appropriate string based on the content language's typographic conventions. This is the default property value, and only needs to be explicitly set in order to override a different inherited value.

hyphenate-limit-chars.description: The `hyphenate-limit-chars` [CSS](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS) property specifies the minimum word length to allow hyphenation of words as well as the minimum number of characters before and after the hyphen.

hyphens.description: The `hyphens` [CSS](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS) property specifies how words should be hyphenated when text wraps across multiple lines.

values.none: Words are not broken at line breaks, even if characters inside the words suggest line break points. Lines will only wrap at whitespace.
values.manual: Default value. Words are broken for line-wrapping only where characters inside the word suggest line break opportunities. See [Suggesting line break opportunities](#suggesting_line_break_opportunities) below for details.
values.auto: The browser is free to automatically break words at appropriate hyphenation points, following whatever rules it chooses. However, suggested line break opportunities (see [Suggesting line break opportunities](#suggesting_line_break_opportunities) below) will override automatic break point selection when present.

image-orientation.description: The `image-orientation` [CSS](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS) property specifies a layout-independent correction to the orientation of an image.

values.none: Does not apply any additional image rotation; the image is oriented as encoded or as other CSS property values dictate.
values.from-image: Default initial value. The [EXIF](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/EXIF) information contained in the image is used to rotate the image appropriately.
values.flip: After rotating by the precededing angle, the image is flipped horizontally. Defaults to 0deg if the angle is ommitted.
values.deg: Represents an angle in [degrees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Degree_%28angle%29). One full circle is `360deg`. Examples: `0deg`, `90deg`, `14.23deg`.
values.grad: Represents an angle in [gradians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gradian). One full circle is `400grad`. Examples: `0grad`, `100grad`, `38.8grad`.
values.rad: Represents an angle in [radians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radian). One full circle is 2π radians which approximates to `6.2832rad`. `1rad` is 180/π degrees. Examples: `0rad`, `1.0708rad`, `6.2832rad`.
values.turn: Represents an angle in a number of turns. One full circle is `1turn`. Examples: `0turn`, `0.25turn`, `1.2turn`.

image-rendering.description: The `image-rendering` [CSS](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS) property sets an image scaling algorithm. The property applies to an element itself, to any images set in its other properties, and to its descendants.

values.auto: The scaling algorithm is UA dependent. Since version 1.9 (Firefox 3.0), Gecko uses _bilinear_ resampling (high quality).
values.smooth: The image should be scaled with an algorithm that maximizes the appearance of the image. In particular, scaling algorithms that "smooth" colors are acceptable, such as bilinear interpolation. This is intended for images such as photos.
values.crisp-edges: The image is scaled with an algorithm such as "nearest neighbor" that preserves contrast and edges in the image. Generally intended for images such as pixel art or line drawings, no blurring or color smoothing occurs.
values.pixelated: The image is scaled with the "nearest neighbor" or similar algorithm to the nearest integer multiple of the original image size, then uses smooth interpolation to bring the image to the final desired size. This is intended to preserve a "pixelated" look without introducing scaling artifacts when the upscaled resolution isn't an integer multiple of the original.

initial-letter.description: The `initial-letter` [CSS](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS) property sets the size and sink for dropped, raised, and sunken initial letters. This property applies to `::first-letter` pseudo-elements and inline-level first children of block containers.

values.normal: No special initial-letter effect. Text behaves as normal.

inline-size.description: The `inline-size` [CSS](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS) property defines the size of an element's block along the [inline axis](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Glossary/Grid_Axis). interactivity.description: The `interactivity` [CSS](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS) property specifies whether an element and its descendant nodes are set to be [inert](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Reference/Global_attributes/inert).

values.auto: Selected elements are in their default state in terms of inertness. This usually means that they are interactive, but this is [not always the case](#default_inertness). This is the default value.
values.inert: Selected elements and their descendants are inert.

interest-delay.description: The `interest-delay` [CSS](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS) property specifies the delay between the user showing interest in an [interest invoker](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Popover_API/Using_interest_invokers) element and the `interest` event firing, and the delay between the user losing interest and the `loseinterest` event firing.

values.normal: Sets the delay to the browser's default delay. This is the initial value.
values.s: Represents a time in seconds. Examples: `0s`, `1.5s`, `-60s`.
values.ms: Represents a time in milliseconds. Examples: `0ms`, `150.25ms`, `-60000ms`.

interest-delay-end.description: The `interest-delay-end` [CSS](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS) property specifies the delay between the user losing interest in an [interest invoker](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Popover_API/Using_interest_invokers) element and the `loseinterest` event firing.

values.normal: Sets the delay to the browser's default delay. This is the initial value.
values.s: Represents a time in seconds. Examples: `0s`, `1.5s`, `-60s`.
values.ms: Represents a time in milliseconds. Examples: `0ms`, `150.25ms`, `-60000ms`.

interest-delay-start.description: The `interest-delay-start` [CSS](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS) property specifies the delay between the user showing interest in an [interest invoker](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Popover_API/Using_interest_invokers) element and the `interest` event firing.

values.normal: Sets the delay to the browser's default delay. This is the initial value.
values.s: Represents a time in seconds. Examples: `0s`, `1.5s`, `-60s`.
values.ms: Represents a time in milliseconds. Examples: `0ms`, `150.25ms`, `-60000ms`.

interpolate-size.description: The `interpolate-size` [CSS](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS) property allows you to enable [animations](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Guides/Animations) and [transitions](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Guides/Transitions) between a `<length-percentage>` value and an `intrinsic size`, `fit-content`, or `max-content`.

values.allow-keywords: Enables [interpolation](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Glossary/Interpolation) between a `length-percentage` value and an intrinsic size value, to allow animation between the two.
values.numeric-only: The default behavior — intrinsic size values cannot be interpolated.

isolation.description: The `isolation` [CSS](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS) property determines whether an element must create a new `stacking context`.

values.auto: A new stacking context is created only if one of the properties applied to the element requires it.
values.isolate: A new stacking context must be created.

justify-content.description: The [CSS](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS) `justify-content` property defines how the browser distributes space between and around content items along the `main axis` of a flex container and the [inline axis](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Glossary/Logical_properties#inline_direction) of grid and multicol containers.

values.start: The items are packed flush to each other toward the start edge of the alignment container in the main axis.
values.end: The items are packed flush to each other toward the end edge of the alignment container in the main axis.
values.flex-start: The items are packed flush to each other toward the start edge of the alignment container on the flex container's main-start side. This only applies to flex layout items. For items that are not children of a flex container, this value is treated like `start`.
values.flex-end: The items are packed flush to each other at the end edge of the alignment container on the flex container's main-end side. This only applies to flex layout items. For items that are not children of a flex container, this value is treated like `end`.
values.center: The items are packed flush to each other toward the center of the alignment container along the main axis.
values.left: The items are packed flush to each other toward the left edge of the alignment container. When the property's horizontal axis is not parallel with the inline axis, such as when [`flex-direction: column;`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Reference/Properties/flex-direction) is set, this value behaves like `start`.
values.right: The items are packed flush to each other toward the right edge of the alignment container in the appropriate axis. If the property's axis is not parallel with the inline axis (in a grid container) or the main-axis (in a flexbox container), this value behaves like `start`.
values.normal: Behaves as `stretch`, except in the case of multi-column containers with a non-`auto` `column-width`, in which case the columns take their specified `column-width` rather than stretching to fill the container. As `stretch` behaves as `start` in flex containers, `normal` also behaves as `start`.
values.space-between: The items are evenly distributed within the alignment container along the main axis. The spacing between each pair of adjacent items is the same. The first item is flush with the main-start edge, and the last item is flush with the main-end edge.
values.space-around: The items are evenly distributed within the alignment container along the main axis. The spacing between each pair of adjacent items is the same. The empty space before the first and after the last item equals half of the space between each pair of adjacent items. If there is only one item, it will be centered.
values.space-evenly: The items are evenly distributed within the alignment container along the main axis. The spacing between each pair of adjacent items, the main-start edge and the first item, and the main-end edge and the last item, are all exactly the same.
values.stretch: If the combined size of the items along the main axis is less than the size of the alignment container, any `auto`-sized items have their size increased equally (not proportionally), while still respecting the constraints imposed by `max-height`/`max-width` (or equivalent functionality), so that the combined size exactly fills the alignment container along the main axis.
values.safe: If the item overflows the alignment container, then the item is aligned as if the alignment mode is `start`. The desired alignment will not be implemented.
values.unsafe: Even if the item overflows the alignment container, the desired alignment will be implemented. Unlike `safe`, which will ignore the desired alignment in favor of preventing overflow.

justify-items.description: The [CSS](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS) `justify-items` property defines the default `justify-self` for all items of the box, giving them all a default way of justifying each box along the appropriate axis.

values.normal: The effect of this keyword is dependent of the layout mode we are in: - In block-level layouts, the keyword is a synonym of `start`. - In absolutely-positioned layouts, the keyword behaves like `start` on _replaced_ absolutely-positioned boxes, and as `stretch` on _all other_ absolutely-positioned boxes. - In table cell layouts, this keyword has no meaning as this property is _ignored_. - In flexbox layouts, this keyword has no meaning as this property is _ignored._ - In grid layouts, this keyword leads to a behavior similar to the one of `stretch`, except for boxes with an aspect ratio or an intrinsic size where it behaves like `start`.
values.start: The item is packed flush to each other toward the start edge of the alignment container in the appropriate axis.
values.end: The item is packed flush to each other toward the end edge of the alignment container in the appropriate axis.
values.flex-start: For items that are not children of a flex container, this value is treated like `start`.
values.flex-end: For items that are not children of a flex container, this value is treated like `end`.
values.self-start: The item is packed flush to the edge of the alignment container of the start side of the item, in the appropriate axis.
values.self-end: The item is packed flush to the edge of the alignment container of the end side of the item, in the appropriate axis.
values.center: The items are packed flush to each other toward the center of the alignment container.
values.left: The items are packed flush to each other toward the left edge of the alignment container. If the property's axis is not parallel with the inline axis, this value behaves like `start`.
values.right: The items are packed flush to each other toward the right edge of the alignment container in the appropriate axis. If the property's axis is not parallel with the inline axis, this value behaves like `start`.
values.baseline: Specifies participation in first- or last-baseline alignment: aligns the alignment baseline of the box's first or last baseline set with the corresponding baseline in the shared first or last baseline set of all the boxes in its baseline-sharing group. The fallback alignment for `first baseline` is `start`, the one for `last baseline` is `end`.
values.stretch: If the combined size of the items is less than the size of the alignment container, any `auto`-sized items have their size increased equally (not proportionally), while still respecting the constraints imposed by `max-height`/`max-width` (or equivalent functionality), so that the combined size exactly fills the alignment container.
values.anchor-center: In the case of [anchor-positioned](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Guides/Anchor_positioning) elements, aligns the items to the center of the associated anchor element in the inline direction. See [Centering on the anchor using `anchor-center`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Guides/Anchor_positioning/Using#centering_on_the_anchor_using_anchor-center).
values.safe: If the size of the item overflows the alignment container, the item is instead aligned as if the alignment mode were `start`.
values.unsafe: Regardless of the relative sizes of the item and alignment container, the given alignment value is honored.
values.legacy: Makes the value inherited by the box descendants. Note that if a descendant has a `justify-self: auto` value, the `legacy` keyword is not considered by the descend, only the `left`, `right`, or `center` value associated to it.

justify-self.description: The [CSS](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS) `justify-self` property sets the way a box is justified inside its alignment container along the appropriate axis.

left.description: The `left` [CSS](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS) property participates in specifying the horizontal position of a [positioned element](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Reference/Properties/position). This `inset property` has no effect on non-positioned elements.

values.auto: Specifies that: - for _absolutely positioned elements_, the position of the element is based on the `right` property, while `width: auto` is treated as a width based on the content; or if `right` is also `auto`, the element is positioned where it should horizontally be positioned if it were a static element. - for _relatively positioned elements_, the distance of the element from its normal position is based on the `right` property; or if `right` is also `auto`, the element is not moved horizontally at all.
values.cap: Equal to the "cap height" (nominal height of capital letters) of the element's `font`.
values.ch: Represents the width or, more precisely, the `advance measure` of the glyph `0` (zero, the Unicode character U+0030) in the element's `font`. In cases where determining the measure of the `0` glyph is impossible or impractical, it must be assumed to be `0.5em` wide by `1em` tall.
values.em: Represents the calculated `font-size` of the element. If used on the `font-size` property itself, it represents the _inherited_ font-size of the element.
values.ex: Equal to the [x-height](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/X-height) of the element's `font`. In fonts with the `x` letter, this is generally the height of lowercase letters in the font; `1ex ≈ 0.5em` in many fonts.
values.ic: Represents the used `advance measure` of the "水" glyph (CJK water ideograph, U+6C34), found in the font used to render it.

values.rch: Equal to the width or the `advance measure` of the glyph `0` (zero, the Unicode character U+0030) in the root element's `font`.

values.rex: Equal to the x-height of the root element's `font`.
values.ric: Equal to the value of [`ic`](#ic) unit on the root element's font.
values.rlh: Equal to the value of [`lh`](#lh) unit on the root element's font. This unit enables length calculations based on the theoretical size of an ideal empty line. However, the size of actual line boxes may differ based on their content.

values.vw: Represents a percentage of the width of the viewport's initial [containing block](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Guides/Display/Containing_block). `1vw` is 1% of the viewport width. values.vmax: Represents in percentage the largest of `vw` and `vh`.
values.vmin: Represents in percentage the smallest of `vw` and `vh`.
values.vb: Represents the percentage of the size of the initial [containing block](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Guides/Display/Containing_block), in the direction of the root element's [block axis](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Guides/Logical_properties_and_values).
values.vi: Represents a percentage of the size of the initial [containing block](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Guides/Display/Containing_block), in the direction of the root element's [inline axis](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Guides/Logical_properties_and_values).

values.cqh: Represents a percentage of the height of the query container. `1cqh` is 1% of the query container's height. For example, if the query container's height is `300px`, then a value of `10cqh` on a property will be `30px`.
values.cqi: Represents a percentage of the inline size of the query container. `1cqi` is 1% of the query container's inline size. For example, if the query container's inline size is `800px`, then a value of `50cqi` on a property will be `400px`.
values.cqb: Represents a percentage of the block size of the query container. `1cqb` is 1% of the query container's block size. For example, if the query container's block size is `300px`, then a value of `10cqb` on a property will be `30px`.
values.cqmin: Represents a percentage of the smaller value of either the query container's inline size or block size. `1cqmin` is 1% of the smaller value of either the query container's inline size or block size. For example, if the query container's inline size is `800px` and its block size is `300px`, then a value of `50cqmin` on a property will be `150px`.
values.cqmax: Represents a percentage of the larger value of either the query container's inline size or block size. `1cqmax` is 1% of the larger value of either the query container's inline size or block size. values.inline: The length of the anchor element's containing block in the inline direction.
values.self-block: The length of the anchor element in the block direction.
values.self-inline: The length of the anchor element in the inline direction.

If present, it overrides the element's `lighting-color` attribute.

values.R: The _red_ component of the color, as a case-insensitive hexadecimal number between `0` and `ff` (255). If there is only one number, it is duplicated: `1` means `11`.

values.G: The _green_ component of the color, as a case-insensitive hexadecimal number between `0` and `ff` (255). If there is only one number, it is duplicated: `c` means `cc`.
values.GG: The _green_ component of the color, as a case-insensitive hexadecimal number between `0` and `ff` (255). If there is only one number, it is duplicated: `c` means `cc`.
values.B: The _blue_ component of the color, as a case-insensitive hexadecimal number between `0` and `ff` (255). If there is only one number, it is duplicated: `9` means `99`.
values.BB: The _blue_ component of the color, as a case-insensitive hexadecimal number between `0` and `ff` (255). If there is only one number, it is duplicated: `9` means `99`.
values.A: The _alpha_ component of the color, indicating its transparency, as a case-insensitive hexadecimal number between `0` and `ff` (255). If there is only one number, it is duplicated: `e` means `ee`. `0`, or `00`, represents a fully transparent color, and `f`, or `ff`, a fully opaque one.

line-break.description: The `line-break` [CSS](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS) property sets how to break lines of Chinese, Japanese, or Korean (CJK) text when working with punctuation and symbols.

values.auto: Break text using the default line break rule.
values.loose: Break text using the least restrictive line break rule. Typically used for short lines, such as in newspapers.
values.normal: Break text using the most common line break rule.
values.strict: Break text using the most stringent line break rule.
values.anywhere: There is a soft wrap opportunity around every typographic character unit, including around any punctuation character or preserved white spaces, or in the middle of words, disregarding any prohibition against line breaks, even those introduced by characters with the GL, WJ, or ZWJ character class or mandated by the `word-break` property. The different wrapping opportunities must not be prioritized. Hyphenation is not applied.

values.none: No list style is used.
values.inside: The marker box is outside the principal block box, as described in the section on the ::marker pseudo-element below.

values.decimal-leading-zero: Decimal numbers, padded by initial zeros.

list-style-image.description: The `list-style-image` [CSS](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS) property sets an image to be used as the list item marker.

values.none: Specifies that no image is used as the marker. If this value is set, the marker defined in will be used instead. This is the default value for `list-style`.

list-style-position.description: The `list-style-position` [CSS](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS) property sets the position of the `::marker` relative to a list item.

values.inside: The `::marker` is the first element among the list item's contents.
values.outside: The `::marker` is outside the principal block box. This is the default value for `list-style`.

list-style-type.description: The `list-style-type` [CSS](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS) property sets the marker (such as a disc, character, or custom counter style) of a list item element.

values.none: No item marker is shown.
values.decimal-leading-zero: Decimal numbers, padded by initial zeros.
values.japanese-formal: Japanese formal numbering to be used in legal or financial documents. The kanjis are designed so that they can't be modified to look like another correct one.
values.disclosure-open: Symbol indicating that a disclosure widget such as `details` is opened.
values.disclosure-closed: Symbol indicating that a disclosure widget, like `details` is closed.
values.symbols(): Allows a counter style to be defined inline.

margin.description: The `margin` [CSS](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS) shorthand property sets the [margin area](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Guides/Box_model/Introduction#margin_area) on all four sides of an element.

values.auto: The browser selects a suitable margin to use. For example, in certain cases this value can be used to center an element.
values.cap: Equal to the "cap height" (nominal height of capital letters) of the element's `font`.
values.ch: Represents the width or, more precisely, the `advance measure` of the glyph `0` (zero, the Unicode character U+0030) in the element's `font`. In cases where determining the measure of the `0` glyph is impossible or impractical, it must be assumed to be `0.5em` wide by `1em` tall.
values.em: Represents the calculated `font-size` of the element. If used on the `font-size` property itself, it represents the _inherited_ font-size of the element.
values.ex: Equal to the [x-height](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/X-height) of the element's `font`. In fonts with the `x` letter, this is generally the height of lowercase letters in the font; `1ex ≈ 0.5em` in many fonts.
values.ic: Represents the used `advance measure` of the "水" glyph (CJK water ideograph, U+6C34), found in the font used to render it.
values.lh: Equal to the computed value of the `line-height` property of the element on which it is used, converted to an absolute length. This unit enables length calculations based on the theoretical size of an ideal empty line. However, the size of actual line boxes may differ based on their content.
values.rcap: Equal to the "cap height" (nominal height of capital letters) of the root element's `font`.
values.rch: Equal to the width or the `advance measure` of the glyph `0` (zero, the Unicode character U+0030) in the root element's `font`.
values.rem: Represents the `font-size` of the root element (typically `html`). When used within the root element `font-size`, it represents its initial value. A common browser default is `16px`, but user-defined preferences may modify this.
values.rex: Equal to the x-height of the root element's `font`.
values.ric: Equal to the value of [`ic`](#ic) unit on the root element's font.
values.rlh: Equal to the value of [`lh`](#lh) unit on the root element's font. This unit enables length calculations based on the theoretical size of an ideal empty line. However, the size of actual line boxes may differ based on their content.
values.vh: Represents a percentage of the height of the viewport's initial [containing block](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Guides/Display/Containing_block). `1vh` is 1% of the viewport height. For example, if the viewport height is `300px`, then a value of `70vh` on a property will be `210px`.
values.vw: Represents a percentage of the width of the viewport's initial [containing block](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Guides/Display/Containing_block). `1vw` is 1% of the viewport width. values.vmin: Represents in percentage the smallest of `vw` and `vh`.

values.block: The length of the anchor element's [containing block](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Guides/Display/Containing_block) in the block direction.

margin-right.description: The `margin-right` [CSS](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS) property sets the [margin area](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Guides/Box_model/Introduction#margin_area) on the right side of an element. A positive value places it farther from its neighbors, while a negative value places it closer.

values.auto: The right margin receives a share of the unused horizontal space, as determined mainly by the layout mode that is used. If the values of `margin-left` and `margin-right` are both `auto`, the calculated space is evenly distributed. This table summarizes the different cases:
values.cap: Equal to the "cap height" (nominal height of capital letters) of the element's `font`.
values.ch: Represents the width or, more precisely, the `advance measure` of the glyph `0` (zero, the Unicode character U+0030) in the element's `font`. In cases where determining the measure of the `0` glyph is impossible or impractical, it must be assumed to be `0.5em` wide by `1em` tall.
values.em: Represents the calculated `font-size` of the element. If used on the `font-size` property itself, it represents the _inherited_ font-size of the element.
values.ex: Equal to the [x-height](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/X-height) of the element's `font`. In fonts with the `x` letter, this is generally the height of lowercase letters in the font; `1ex ≈ 0.5em` in many fonts.
values.ic: Represents the used `advance measure` of the "水" glyph (CJK water ideograph, U+6C34), found in the font used to render it.
values.lh: Equal to the computed value of the `line-height` property of the element on which it is used, converted to an absolute length. This unit enables length calculations based on the theoretical size of an ideal empty line. However, the size of actual line boxes may differ based on their content.
values.rcap: Equal to the "cap height" (nominal height of capital letters) of the root element's `font`.
values.rch: Equal to the width or the `advance measure` of the glyph `0` (zero, the Unicode character U+0030) in the root element's `font`.
values.rem: Represents the `font-size` of the root element (typically `html`). When used within the root element `font-size`, it represents its initial value. A common browser default is `16px`, but user-defined preferences may modify this.
values.rex: Equal to the x-height of the root element's `font`.
values.ric: Equal to the value of [`ic`](#ic) unit on the root element's font.
values.rlh: Equal to the value of [`lh`](#lh) unit on the root element's font. This unit enables length calculations based on the theoretical size of an ideal empty line. However, the size of actual line boxes may differ based on their content.
values.vh: Represents a percentage of the height of the viewport's initial [containing block](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Guides/Display/Containing_block). `1vh` is 1% of the viewport height. For example, if the viewport height is `300px`, then a value of `70vh` on a property will be `210px`.
values.vw: Represents a percentage of the width of the viewport's initial [containing block](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Guides/Display/Containing_block). `1vw` is 1% of the viewport width. For example, if the viewport width is `800px`, then a value of `50vw` on a property will be `400px`.
values.vmax: Represents in percentage the largest of `vw` and `vh`.
values.vmin: Represents in percentage the smallest of `vw` and `vh`.
values.vb: Represents the percentage of the size of the initial [containing block](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Guides/Display/Containing_block), in the direction of the root element's [block axis](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Guides/Logical_properties_and_values).
values.vi: Represents a percentage of the size of the initial [containing block](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Guides/Display/Containing_block), in the direction of the root element's [inline axis](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Guides/Logical_properties_and_values).

values.cqh: Represents a percentage of the height of the query container. `1cqh` is 1% of the query container's height. For example, if the query container's height is `300px`, then a value of `10cqh` on a property will be `30px`.
values.cqi: Represents a percentage of the inline size of the query container. `1cqi` is 1% of the query container's inline size. For example, if the query container's inline size is `800px`, then a value of `50cqi` on a property will be `400px`.
values.cqb: Represents a percentage of the block size of the query container. `1cqb` is 1% of the query container's block size. For example, if the query container's block size is `300px`, then a value of `10cqb` on a property will be `30px`.
values.cqmin: Represents a percentage of the smaller value of either the query container's inline size or block size. `1cqmin` is 1% of the smaller value of either the query container's inline size or block size. For example, if the query container's inline size is `800px` and its block size is `300px`, then a value of `50cqmin` on a property will be `150px`.
values.cqmax: Represents a percentage of the larger value of either the query container's inline size or block size. `1cqmax` is 1% of the larger value of either the query container's inline size or block size. margin-trim.description: The `margin-trim` property allows the container to trim the margins of its children where they adjoin the container's edges.

values.none: Margins are not trimmed by the container.
values.block: Margins provided to the block children where they adjoin the container's edges are trimmed to zero without affecting the margins provided to the container.
values.block-start: Margin of the first block child with the container's edge is trimmed to zero.
values.block-end: Margin of last block child with the container's edge is trimmed to zero.
values.inline: Margins provided to the inline children where they adjoin the container's edges are trimmed to zero, without affecting the spacing at the beginning and end of the row.
values.inline-start: Margin between the container's edge and the first inline child is trimmed to zero.
values.inline-end: Margin between the container's edge and the last inline child is trimmed to zero.

marker.description: The `marker` [CSS](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS) property points to a marker that will be drawn on the first, middle, and last vertices of the element's path; that is, at all of its vertices. The marker must have been defined using an SVG `marker` element, and can only be referenced with a `<url>` value. The value of the CSS property overrides any values of the `marker-start`, `marker`, and `marker-end` attributes in the SVG.

values.none: This means no marker will be drawn at each vertex of the element's path.
values.url(): Indicates that the <marker> element referenced will be used.

marker-end.description: The `marker-end` [CSS](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS) property points to a marker that will be drawn on the last vertex of the element's path; that is, at its ending vertex. The marker must have been defined using an SVG `marker` element, and can only be referenced with a `<url>` value. The value of the CSS property overrides any values of the `marker-end` attribute in the SVG.

values.none: This means no marker will be drawn at the last vertex of the element's path.
values.url(): Indicates that the <marker> element referenced will be used.

marker-mid.description: The `marker-mid` [CSS](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS) property points to a marker that will be drawn on the middle vertices of the element's path; that is, at each of its vertices between the start and end vertices. The marker must have been defined using an SVG `marker` element, and can only be referenced with a `<url>` value. The value of the CSS property overrides any values of the `marker-mid` attribute in the SVG.

values.none: This means no marker will be drawn at each middle vertex of the element's path.
values.url(): Indicates that the <marker> element referenced will be used.

marker-start.description: The `marker-start` [CSS](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS) property points to a marker that will be drawn on the first vertex of the element's path; that is, at its starting vertex. The marker must have been defined using an SVG `marker` element, and can only be referenced with a `<url>` value. The value of the CSS property overrides any values of the `marker-start` attribute in the SVG.

values.none: This means no marker will be drawn at the first vertex of the element's path.
values.url(): Indicates that the <marker> element referenced will be used.

values.px: One pixel. For screen displays, it traditionally represents one `device pixel` (dot). However, for _printers_ and _high-resolution screens_, one CSS pixel implies multiple device pixels. `1px` = `1in / 96`.
values.none: This keyword is interpreted as a transparent black image layer.
values.url(): Reference to a <mask element or to a CSS image.
values.alpha: Indicates that the alpha (transparency) values of the mask image should be used.
values.luminance: Indicates that the [luminance (brightness)](#understanding_luminance) values of the mask image should be used.
values.match-source: Indicates that the type of mask is determined by the source. This is the default property value. - If the `mask-image` references an SVG `mask`, its `mask-type` property value is used, or its `mask-type` attribute, if present. If neither is explicitly set, this value defaults to `luminance`. - If the mask image source is an `image` or a `gradient`, the `alpha` values of the mask image are used.
values.auto: Use alpha values if 'mask-image' is an image, luminance if a <mask> element or a CSS image.
values.repeat: The image is repeated as much as needed to cover the whole mask painting area. Mask images along the edges are clipped when the size of the [mask origin box](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Reference/Properties/mask-origin) is not an exact multiple of the mask image's size.
values.space: The mask image is repeated as many times as possible without clipping. If the element's origin size is at least twice the size as the mask image's size in the associated dimension, the `mask-position` property is ignored and the first and last images are positioned at the edges of the mask origin container. If the mask origin box is not an exact multiple of the mask image's size, whitespace is distributed evenly between the repeated mask images.
values.round: The mask image is repeated as many times as possible in its original dimensions. If the size of the mask origin box is not an exact multiple of the mask image's size, all mask images will be rescaled, [shrinking or stretching](#rounded_repetitions) to ensure no repetitions are clipped.
values.no-repeat: The mask image is not repeated (and hence the mask painting area will not necessarily be entirely covered). The position of the non-repeated mask image is defined by the `mask-position` CSS property.
values.repeat-x: The equivalent of `repeat no-repeat`. The image is repeated in the horizontal direction as many times as needed to cover the width of the mask painting area. Mask images along the right or left edges, or both depending on the `mask-position` value, will be clipped if the width of the mask origin box is not an exact multiple of the mask image's width.
values.repeat-y: The equivalent of `no-repeat repeat`. The image is repeated in the vertical direction as many times as needed to cover the height of the mask painting area. Mask images along the top or bottom edges, or both depending on the `mask-position` value, will be clipped if the height of the mask origin box is not an exact multiple of the mask image's height.
values.content-box: The painted content is clipped to the content box.
values.padding-box: The painted content is clipped to the padding box.
values.border-box: The painted content is clipped to the border box.
values.fill-box: The painted content is clipped to the object bounding box.
values.stroke-box: The painted content is clipped to the stroke bounding box.
values.view-box: Uses the nearest SVG viewport as reference box. If a [`viewBox`](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/SVG/Reference/Attribute/viewBox) attribute is specified for the element creating the SVG viewport, the reference box is positioned at the origin of the coordinate system established by the `viewBox` attribute and the dimension of the reference box is set to the width and height values of the `viewBox` attribute.
values.no-clip: The painted content is not clipped.
values.border: This keyword behaves the same as `border-box`.
values.padding: This keyword behaves the same as `padding-box`.
values.content: This keyword behaves the same as `content-box`.
values.text: This keyword clips the mask image to the text of the element.
values.contain: Scales the mask image up or down, while preserving its aspect-ratio, making the mask as large as possible within its container without cropping or stretching it. If the mask image is smaller than the container, the mask will tile, or repeat, unless the `mask-repeat` property is set to `no-repeat`.
values.cover: Scales the mask image to the smallest possible size to fill the container while preserving its aspect ratio. If the aspect ratio of the mask image differs from the element, it will be cropped vertically or horizontally.
values.add: The associated mask image is placed over all mask layers below it (with the corresponding compositing operators applied). This is the default value.
values.subtract: The associated mask image is placed, where it falls outside of all mask layers below it (with the corresponding compositing operators applied).
values.intersect: The parts of the associated mask image that overlap all composited mask layers below it replace those previously composited layers.
values.exclude: The non-overlapping regions of the associated mask image and the mask layers below it, with their corresponding compositing operators applied, are combined.

values.stretch: The source image's edge regions are stretched to fill the gap between each border.
values.repeat: The source image's edge regions are tiled (repeated) to fill the gap between each border. Tiles may be clipped to achieve the proper fit.
values.round: The source image's edge regions are tiled (repeated) to fill the gap between each border. Tiles may be stretched to achieve the proper fit.
values.space: The source image's edge regions are tiled (repeated) to fill the gap between each border. Extra space will be distributed in between tiles to achieve the proper fit.

mask-border-slice.description: The `mask-border-slice` [CSS](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS) property divides the image set by `mask-border-source` into regions. These regions are used to form the components of an element's [mask border](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Reference/Properties/mask-border).

values.fill: Preserves the middle image region. Its width and height are sized to match the top and left image regions, respectively.

mask-border-source.description: The `mask-border-source` [CSS](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS) property sets the source image used to create an element's [mask border](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Reference/Properties/mask-border).

values.none: No mask border is used.

mask-border-width.description: The `mask-border-width` [CSS](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS) property sets the width of an element's [mask border](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/CSS/Reference/Properties/mask-border).

values.auto: The width of the mask border is made equal to the intrinsic width or height (whichever is applicable) of the corresponding `mask-border-slice`. If the image does not have the required intrinsic dimension, the corresponding `border-width` is used instead.
